title: Resolve rolling-aggregation proration skew and duplicate credit lines in billing exports
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Summary: The nightly billing export and reconciliation pipeline is producing incorrect proration on mid-cycle invoices and duplicate credit lines for customers who hit rate limits around rolling aggregation window boundaries. Root cause appears to be the combination of: (1) a sliding aggregation window implemented in the usage-aggregator that can include partial hours from two windows, (2) late-arriving webhook retries that re-ingest the same usage with slightly different timestamps, and (3) the credits apportioner logic which currently de-duplicates only by raw event_id and not by normalized usage footprint. Symptoms: duplicated rate-limit credits in NetSuite exports, proration amounts that don't match Stripe invoice lines, and a rise in customer billing disputes for affected accounts. This ticket tracks investigation, fix design, and rollout for the reconciler, aggregator, and export composer.
reproduction_steps: Simulate heavy per-minute requests to a single API key across an hour boundary (e.g., 10:59:30 -> 11:00:30) while exceeding rate limits.
Replay a webhook delivery with a 90s delay (duplicate event_id stripped, but timestamp differs by +1s).
Run nightly reconciler job staging-run: billing-reconciler-staging-2026-03-01 and compare netSuite-export CSV and stripe-lines.json outputs.
Query: SELECT count(*) FROM aggregated_usage WHERE key_id='X' AND window_start BETWEEN '2026-02-28T10:59:00Z' AND '2026-02-28T11:01:00Z'; compare to raw_events where attempted_at in same range.
observed_logs_and_artifacts: Github PR with current hotfix attempt: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/2487
analysis_notes: Aggregator uses a [start, start+interval) sliding window with microsecond timestamps; this allows the same raw event to be included in adjacent windows if timestamp normalization differs by clock skew or retry offset.
De-dup path in credits apportioner only checks raw_event.event_id; webhook replays can create new event_ids when proxied through the gateway, so duplicates slip through.

Proration calculation depends on per-window usage buckets; when a single user’s usage is split across two windows, the apportioner rounds each partial window independently, producing small fractional cents that sum to an observable mismatch against Stripe’s single-line proration math.
Timezone/DST is not the cause for most cases — most affected customers are UTC, but clock skew and retry jitter are.

Customer complaints originate mostly from mid-market accounts with reserved capacity where rounding differences exceed internal tolerance and show up as invoice mismatches via NetSuite reconciliation rules.
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Decided to normalize event timestamps at ingestion to second precision to reduce cross-window duplication (Jonah R., Aisha M., Priya S.).

2026-03-03: Agreed to extend de-duplication keys in apportioner to include (normalized_timestamp_floor, customer_id, usage_signature) in addition to event_id to catch gateway-replayed events (Engineering architecture review).
2026-03-04: Rejected full-hour-alignment approach due to increased latency of rounding; chosen approach minimizes data mutation while preserving cost accuracy.
2026-03-06: Plan to add a reconciliation post-process that collapses near-duplicate credit lines using fuzzy-equality on cents and aggregated token counts for the NetSuite composer.
acceptance_criteria: NetSuite exports for affected staging accounts show no duplicate credit lines for the same rate-limit incident across a 3-day test window.
Proration amounts in produced stripe-lines.json match Stripe's invoice proration calculation within 1 cent for 99.9% of test cases.
Nightly reconciler job latency increase <= 5% after changes and memory usage within existing worker limits.
Runbook updated and on-call PagerDuty rotation notified; rollback path validated via feature flag.
work_items: Modify ingestion pipeline: normalize timestamps to second precision and add ingest-time canonical_id (Aisha)
Update credits apportioner de-dup logic to include normalized timestamp floor + usage signature (Jonah)
Add post-export collapse step in NetSuite composer to merge near-duplicate line items (Priya)
Add unit+integration tests for retry/replay scenarios and cross-window aggregation (Engineering)
Run 72-hour canary on staging with synthetic workloads and escalate if mismatch rate > 0.1% (SRE/Oncall)
Create customer communication template for any customers with invoices affected in last 2 billing cycles (CS/Finance)
Create migration job to re-run reconciler for last 7 days of high-risk accounts if post-fix verification passes (Data Eng)
Ship feature-flag guarded rollout with metrics: duplicate_credit_lines_pct, proration_diff_cents_p99 (Release)
